title: Nuclear Chemistry and Radioactivity

cards.b: Ordinary chemistry rearranges electrons. Nuclear chemistry changes the nucleus itself, releasing millions of times more energy per atom. It powers stars, hospital scanners, nuclear plants and weapons, and it dates ancient bones.

Henri Becquerel (1896) found uranium emitted rays; Marie and Pierre Curie discovered polonium and radium (1898) and named the phenomenon radioactivity. Unstable nuclei decay to become stable. The Curies and Becquerel shared the 1903 Physics Nobel, and Marie Curie won the 1911 Chemistry Nobel.

• Alpha (α): a helium nucleus (2 protons, 2 neutrons). Heavy, stopped by paper or skin. Dangerous if swallowed.
  • Beta (β): a fast electron from a neutron changing to a proton. Stopped by thin aluminium.
  • Gamma (γ): high-energy light. Needs thick lead or concrete.

Alpha decay example: U-238 → Th-234 + He-4. Mass numbers (238 = 234 + 4) and atomic numbers (92 = 90 + 2) both balance.
The half-life is the time for half the radioactive atoms to decay. It is fixed for an isotope: iodine-131 about 8 days, carbon-14 about 5,730 years, uranium-238 about 4.5 billion years.

Fission: a heavy nucleus splits. Hahn and Strassmann found it in 1938; Meitner and Frisch explained it. U-235 + n → Ba-141 + Kr-92 + 3n + energy. The released neutrons trigger a chain reaction.

Fusion: light nuclei merge, as hydrogen into helium in the Sun. Einstein's E = mc2 explains the energy: a little mass vanishes and becomes a lot of energy.

• Power: nuclear reactors give low-carbon electricity.
  • Medicine: iodine-131 for thyroid, technetium-99m for scans, cobalt-60 for radiotherapy.
  • Dating: carbon-14 for remains up to about 50,000 years old.
  • Risks: radiation damages DNA; waste stays hazardous for long periods; accidents (Chernobyl 1986, Fukushima 2011).

80 g of a radioisotope with half-life 3 days. After 9 days: 9/3 = 3 half-lives: 80 → 40 → 20 → 10 g.

A bone has 25 percent of its original carbon-14. That is 2 half-lives, so age = 2 x 5,730 = 11,460 years.

Balance: Radium-226 (Z = 88) alpha decays to radon (Z = ?): Z = 86, mass 222.

• Radioactive does not mean glowing green.
  • Reactors cannot explode like bombs. Fuel is far less enriched.
  • Radiation is not always man-made. Bananas, granite and cosmic rays all give small doses.
  • Half-life does not mean it is gone after two half-lives. 25 percent remains.

Homi J. Bhabha founded the Atomic Energy Commission (1948) and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research. In 1954 he set out India's three-stage nuclear programme: (1) natural-uranium heavy-water reactors, (2) fast breeder reactors using plutonium, (3) thorium-based reactors, to use India's large thorium reserves in monazite sands. BARC, Trombay carries on the research; Kudankulam in Tamil Nadu is among India's biggest plants.

• Alpha, beta and gamma differ in mass, charge and penetration.
  • Half-life is constant: halves each period.
  • Fission splits, fusion joins nuclei; mass becomes energy (E = mc2).
